title: A landing/Overview surface must not omit a visible health signal
requirement: Where a Clank has both a landing/Overview page and one or more dedicated health/status pages elsewhere, the landing page MUST include at least some visible indicator of source/collector health (a count of degraded/failed sources, a status strip, or equivalent) — an operator MUST NOT be able to land on the Overview and reasonably believe the Clank is fine while a dedicated status page elsewhere shows an active failure.
rationale: Not part of the operator's original example set for this pass — surfaced independently while comparing Overview semantics across the fleet. 6 of 9 surveyed Clanks already do this (watch-clank's healthy/degraded/never-run buckets, oem-radar's crawl-status bar, tablet-clank's sources-healthy/total card, feature-phone-clank's Overall Health tile, smartwatch-clank's health strip, korean-tech-wire's single-page design which necessarily includes it). 3 do not: chinese-tech-wire's Newsroom, semiconductor-intelligence's Editorial Inbox landing tab, and smartphone-clank's Home page all explicitly show no health signal, deferring entirely to a separate /health or /metrics page. This is weaker evidence than the other Pass 2 candidates — the 3 gap cases are all multi-page apps that made a deliberate separation-of-concerns choice, which is a defensible design, not obviously a bug the way COM-008's or COM-011's counter-evidence is. Recommendation reflects that: this is a real, evidenced pattern, but with a meaningfully weaker case than COM-008/009/010/011, and 3 current non-conformers who chose this on purpose rather than by omission.
forbidden: An Overview/landing page with zero health signal when a dedicated health page elsewhere shows an active degradation or failure
acceptance: The landing page shows at least one health-derived value (a count, a badge, a status strip) sourced from the same data a dedicated health page would show
It does not need to duplicate the full health table — a summary signal is sufficient

evidence.summary: Six Clanks surface a health signal on the landing page.

Three Clanks deliberately keep the landing page lean and put health only on a separate page — a defensible design choice, not clearly a defect, which is why this rule's recommendation is weaker than the others in this pass.

notes: Pass 2 candidate, recommendation QUALIFIED (see docs/gui-ratification-pass-2.md) — weaker evidence base than COM-008/009/010/011, and the 3 non-conforming Clanks appear to have chosen this deliberately as a separation-of-concerns design, not by oversight.
